title: Summarise a slice of an int array with a primitive stream

blocks.text: `Arrays.stream(int[] array, int from, int to)` streams a slice of a primitive array as an `IntStream`, with no boxing. Primitive streams bring numeric terminal operations with them: `sum()`, `average()` and `summaryStatistics()`.

Write `RangeSummary.summarize(int[] values, int from, int to)`. It returns a `Summary(long count, long sum, double average)` for the values at indexes `from` (inclusive) to `to` (exclusive). The indexes are always valid for the array.
An empty slice has a summary too (its average is `0.0`), and a slice of large values may add up to more than an `int` holds.

cases.says: It gives the count, sum and average of the values from index from up to, not including, index to.
A slice with from == to is empty, not an error: count 0, sum 0, average 0.0.
The sum is a long, so a sum past Integer.MAX_VALUE is exact instead of wrapping.

concepts: An empty range such as IntStream.range(n, n) or Arrays.stream(arr, i, i) is an empty stream, not an error.
Primitive streams add numeric terminal operations such as sum(), average() and summaryStatistics().
Arrays.stream turns a primitive array, or a slice of one, into a primitive stream with no boxing.
